sec: Hepatitis D virus: coinfection vs superinfection, antibodies, prognosis, HEV-in-pregnancy note

items.q: Fill up: 'Hepatitis D Virus — Delta virus, ______'.
items.exp: 'Hepatitis D Virus : Delta virus, RNA'. (Book p1044)

items.q: HDV — match — 1) Coinfection 2) Superinfection … A) Chronic HBV + acute hepatitis D (acute on chronic) B) Acute HBV infection + acute HDV infection
items.exp: 'Coinfection : Acute HBV infection + Acute HDV infection'; 'Superinfection (Acute on chronic) : Chronic HBV + Acute Hepatitis D'. (Book p1044)

items.q: Antibody patterns — match — 1) Coinfection 2) Superinfection … A) HBsAg +ve with anti-HDV IgM B) Anti-HBc IgM +ve with anti-HDV IgM +ve
items.exp: Coinfection prints 'Anti HBc IgM +ve' and 'Anti HDV IgM +ve'; superinfection prints 'HBsAg +ve' and 'Anti HDV IgM'. (Book p1044)

items.q: Risk of fulminant hepatitis printed in the coinfection column?
items.exp: 'Other features : Chances of fulminant hepatitis 5-20%'. (Book p1044)

items.q: What long-term outcome is printed down the superinfection column?
items.exp: 'Chronic HDV related cirrhosis' is the end-point of the superinfection column. (Book p1044)

items.q: Which autoantibody is printed in the hepatitis D page?
items.exp: 'Anti LKM-3 Antibody' appears against the delta agent and again in the superinfection column. (Book p1044)

items.q: Judge the hepatitis D table: I Coinfection is acute HBV plus acute HDV with anti-HBc IgM positive. II Superinfection is acute HDV on chronic HBV and carries a bad prognosis with chronic HDV cirrhosis.
items.exp: Coinfection = both infections acute with anti-HBc IgM +ve; superinfection = acute on chronic, '(Bad prognosis)' → 'Chronic HDV related cirrhosis'. (Book p1044)

items.q: The closing note on this page flags a high risk of fulminant hepatic failure for which virus in pregnancy?
items.exp: 'Note : HEV in pregnancy also has a high risk of fulminant hepatic failure.' (Book p1044)

items.q: A patient with known chronic hepatitis B suddenly deteriorates with jaundice and tests anti-HDV IgM positive. Which pattern and prognosis does the page print?
opts: Superinfection — bad prognosis with chronic HDV-related cirrhosis
Coinfection — anti-HBc IgM positive with 5-20% fulminant risk
Resolved HDV with anti-HDV IgG only
HAV superinfection with no chronic sequelae
items.exp: Chronic HBV + acute hepatitis D is superinfection (acute on chronic), which the page labels '(Bad prognosis)' → 'Chronic HDV related cirrhosis'. (Book p1044)

items.q: Which is NOT printed in the superinfection column?
items.exp: Anti-HBc IgM positivity is printed in the coinfection column, not the superinfection column. (Book p1044)
